# ISSUE-88 implementation plan

Reuse coordinator-recorded passing validation only for the exact checkpoint content and validation context. Keep validation commands explicit, CI unconditional, and publication fenced.

**Shape: Involved.** The change joins checkpoint staging, trusted validation, fenced artifact recording, two submission paths, and provenance without changing publication behavior.

## What we know

- `workspace.Checkpoint` strips active pointers, rejects tracked/staged recovery output, and stages the candidate before committing (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:363`). `stageCheckpointFiles` enumerates cached and nonignored untracked literal paths and excludes `.swarm/active-output` (`internal/workspace/timeout_output.go:30`). Comparing HEAD before checkpoint would miss valid uncommitted changes.
- Pointer cleanup handles untracked instruction files containing only a pointer specially; matching only the stripping regex is insufficient (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:835`).
- Validation loads policy exclusively from the approved base and emits metadata containing only base/head today (`internal/validation/validator.go:78`, `:224`, `:234`). Artifact metadata is already an extensible string map (`internal/contract/types.go:58`).
- Issue validation records through the fenced manager (`internal/cli/validate.go:76`); the issue/PR work engine also invokes the same validator (`internal/workflow/engine.go:877`).
- Issue submit checkpoints then always validates (`internal/cli/submit.go:127`). PR submit always calls `Service.validate`, then reacquires the claim for final head checks and publication (`internal/pr/service.go:1017`). PR explicit validation requires a clean recorded revision (`internal/pr/service.go:970`); supporting dirty explicit PR validation is outside this task.
- General artifact updates accept contributor payloads through the fork coordinator (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:386`, `internal/lease/manager.go:1384`). A producer string or caller-provided metadata marker cannot establish trusted origin.
- Issue PR descriptions embed artifacts (`internal/cli/submit.go:281`); PR revisions project artifacts into a managed description section (`internal/pr/review_projection.go:17`).
- CLI version defaults to `dev` and may become `dev+dirty` (`internal/cli/version.go:12`). `make check` runs formatting checks, vet, staticcheck, and race tests (`Makefile:44`).

## What we're assuming

- Hashing the exact trusted policy file bytes with SHA-256 is sufficient and intentionally conservative: cosmetic changes invalidate reuse. Verify the existing trusted loader's file selection in step 2; hash the same bytes it parses, including its existing missing-policy behavior.
- Existing candidate staging semantics should remain authoritative, including tracked generated files and Git filters. Establish parity with actual checkpoints in step 1 instead of creating a new exclusion list.

## Open questions

- Which staging edge cases require special handling for index flags or Git filters? Step 1's parity tests answer this using temporary Git repositories.
- Checks or an external editor may alter content during validation. Step 2 compares fingerprints before and after checks; a changed candidate must never receive a reusable fingerprint for content that was not checked. Existing submit cleanliness checks remain mandatory.
- This planning snapshot has no `.git` directory and `rg` is unavailable (inspection command output); runtime Git tests and `make check` belong to implementation/CI in a normal checkout. This does not block implementation or omit an acceptance criterion.

## Design and alternatives

Use artifact metadata for the fingerprint and a coordinator-only recording path for eligibility. Reject a HEAD-only cache because validate can run before checkpoint. Reject a separate persistent cache because fenced state already holds validation evidence. Reject trusting artifact metadata alone because imported artifacts can carry arbitrary fields. Fork mode continues to validate at submit; it may record fingerprint values but cannot create reusable authority.

### Files and symbols

- `internal/workspace/validation_tree.go` (new): `CheckpointTree` helper; `internal/workspace/timeout_output.go`: factor shared staging enumeration/environment handling used by `stageCheckpointFiles`; keep `Checkpoint` semantics intact. New `validation_tree_test.go` and existing checkpoint tests verify parity.
- `internal/validation/fingerprint.go` (new): fingerprint encoding/parsing, exact-match eligibility, trusted policy digest, and reused report construction. `validator.go`: extend `ValidateOptions` with coordinator version/claim context and attach fingerprint only to stable successful runs. Add fingerprint tests and extend validator tests.
- `internal/lease/manager.go`: add `RecordTrustedValidation` (coordinator-only fenced write) and strip reserved reuse authority from general `UpdateArtifact` inputs. Add manager regression tests. Fork requests retain existing transport and cannot call the trusted writer; gateway-backed trusted recording falls back to ordinary, ineligible recording.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go`: thread version via `WorkOptions` and use trusted validation recording for completed checks. `internal/cli/work.go`, `node.go`, `pr.go`: supply `Version` to work/service contexts, including nested PR work execution. `internal/pr/service.go`: add version context to `Service`, record explicit PR validation, and add submit-only reuse selection to the existing claim-held validation flow.
- `internal/cli/validate.go`, `submit.go`: supply context, record trusted results, choose reuse only after checkpoint, and report reuse. `internal/cli/pr.go`: render reuse details for PR submit. Extend CLI/service/workflow tests; add `internal/cli/validation_reuse_test.go`.
- `internal/pr/review_projection.go` and `internal/cli/submit.go`: use the reused artifact body/summary in existing description attachments; preserve human PR text.
- `README.md`, `docs/developer.md`, `docs/WORKFLOWS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/project.md`, `docs/fork-mode.md`: update relevant validation/submission wording, especially developer.md's unconditional rerun statement. No protected files or schema edits.

## Implementation sequence

1. Implement checkpoint-equivalent tree computation through an exclusively created private temporary index. Seed it from the actual index when present (preserving staged-only state), use the shared cached/untracked literal staging rules, and apply pointer cleanup to temporary index blobs only. Match checkpoint handling for missing/deleted instruction files, tracked empty files, and untracked pointer-only files; reject nonregular instruction paths just as checkpoint does. Use hardened Git commands; set `GIT_INDEX_FILE` only on these commands after credential/environment sanitization. Do not refresh/write the real index or mutate candidate files. Preserve blob modes and Git clean-filter semantics. Reject recovery output as checkpoint does. Clean up the temporary directory and lock on all exits; temporary Git objects are acceptable.
2. Define metadata keys for candidate tree, approved base, SHA-256 of trusted required-checks policy, claim ID, and swarm version. Read policy from the approved base, never candidate YAML. Capture the candidate fingerprint before checks and verify it after checks before granting eligibility; preserve existing FAIL/error behavior. Missing/invalid context or unstable content means no reusable fingerprint. CI never consults reuse. Keep metadata backward compatible; no contract schema change.
3. Establish trusted origin at recording: the new manager method stamps reserved origin and current lease owner/claim after its existing CAS fence, while ordinary artifact imports cannot retain those reserved fields. Bind eligibility to current owner as well as claim; reject fork/gateway/imported artifacts. Record FAIL normally so it replaces earlier PASS evidence. Preserve tester guidance and attestations. Add adversarial tests before integrating selection.
4. Pass actual CLI version and current claim context through issue validate, issue/PR work validation, and PR validate. Treat empty, `dev`, and `dev+dirty` as ineligible for reuse. Library callers without a version safely retain existing validation behavior. Explicit validate always executes checks.
5. After issue submit creates its checkpoint, compare its actual tree with the latest authoritative validation artifact. Require exact PASS, trusted origin, owner, claim, base, policy digest, version, and tree. Missing/malformed values or any mismatch take the existing validation path; policy loading errors retain existing fail-closed behavior. For PR submit, perform the same decision inside the existing claim-held validation preparation/approval flow, without relaxing clean revision checks. Preserve final claim reacquisition, approval checks, clean/head checks, exact-old-remote-head publication, and CAS.
6. On reuse, retain the original check evidence and source timestamp/digest, set report head to the current checkpoint, and record an explicitly reused validation artifact through the fenced trusted writer. Add reuse metadata and a summary/body stating the original run time, age, and short tree SHA. Preserve the original source time across repeated reuse rather than resetting its age. Print a concise reuse message; use stderr for prose in JSON mode and expose reuse details in the structured report. Ensure both PR description paths display the reused evidence without implying checks ran again.
7. Update scoped docs to explain automatic reuse for unchanged released-build validation, mismatch/dev/fork fallback, unchanged CI, and visible reuse provenance. Verify examples against registered commands; add no flags. Run the mapped tests and required checks.

No changes to CI, validation speed, harness policy, claim semantics, or unrelated follow-up features are planned.

# ISSUE-88 test plan

Use real temporary Git repositories and local tracker/claim fixtures; count required-check executions with a marker outside the candidate file set. Inject a release version and a controlled clock in tests. Never use candidate-controlled metadata as a trusted fixture without going through the coordinator recording API.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Passing artifact records checkpoint tree, base, trusted policy digest, claim, and version without touching index/worktree | Workspace table tests compare `CheckpointTree` to `Checkpoint`'s actual commit tree for staged, unstaged, partially staged, new, deleted, renamed, executable, ignored and tracked ignored files; unusual literal filenames; active pointers in tracked and untracked AGENTS/CLAUDE files including pointer-only files; recovery output exclusions/rejections. Compare index bytes, staged diff, worktree bytes/modes, HEAD and status before/after fingerprint success and failure. Include nonregular instruction paths, temporary cleanup, and configured clean filters. Validator tests verify all metadata values, SHA-256 of approved-base policy despite candidate edits, no reuse eligibility on FAIL or content-changing checks. |
| 2. Both submit paths reuse only exact matching PASS; all other cases validate normally | Table-driven eligibility tests vary each bound field independently, plus missing/malformed metadata, untrusted source, owner, and FAIL. Issue CLI integration: validate real uncommitted changes, then submit checkpoints the same tree and check execution count stays one. PR service/CLI integration: validate a clean recorded revision then submit; count stays one. Edit issue content after validate; submission runs checks again. For PR changes, record the new revision through existing staging flow and verify old evidence cannot satisfy submit. Repeat fallback tests with changed base, policy digest, claim, version; assert validation errors remain errors and publication is blocked on fallback failure. |
| 3. Dev builds never reuse | Eligibility and issue/PR submit tests for `dev`, `dev+dirty`, and empty library version run checks again; released matching version reuses. Keep existing version-resolution tests passing. |
| 4. Output, artifact, and PR description disclose reuse with age and short tree | With a fixed clock, assert issue and PR submit text names reuse, original age, and short tree SHA. Assert reused artifact retains source run evidence/time and clearly says reused. Inspect initial issue Draft PR body and PR revision's managed evidence section. JSON output remains parseable, prose goes to stderr, structured report carries reuse data; repeated reuse preserves original age. Human-written PR title/body outside managed evidence remain intact. |
| 5. Regression scenarios, nondestructive index handling, make check | Run all above matrices through both submission entry points where applicable. Extend existing stale claim, concurrent remote update, empty submit, and candidate-changed-during-validation tests so reuse cannot relax them. Add fork/import spoof tests: copied metadata and producer, old claim, and gateway artifacts cannot establish reusable authority; fork submits execute checks. CI/repo validate executes checks regardless of prior evidence. Run `make check` and approved direct checks below. |

## Targeted commands after implementation

```bash
go test ./internal/workspace -run 'Checkpoint|ValidationTree|RecoveryOutput|ActivePointer'
go test ./internal/validation -run 'Fingerprint|Reuse|Validate'
go test ./internal/lease ./internal/fork -run 'Validation|Artifact|ClaimFence'
go test ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/workflow -run 'Validation|Reuse|Submit|Work'
```

Use the same execution-counter fixtures to prove checks actually ran or were skipped; a PASS summary alone is insufficient. Existing adversarial tests must remain unchanged in strength. New security regression cases must fail on the old implementation or on an implementation that accepts forged reuse authority.

## Required implementation validation

Run the approved checks directly and the acceptance-required aggregate:

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

For changed documentation, verify relative links/anchors and syntax-check changed bash examples with `bash -n`; inspect Cobra registrations in `internal/cli/validate.go`, `submit.go`, and `pr.go` for every mentioned command or flag. Read the edited prose for clear reuse/fallback/CI behavior and accurate fork behavior.

This plan-only snapshot lacks Git metadata, so no implementation tests or make checks are claimed as executed. All acceptance criteria have repository-local automated coverage planned; live GitHub and container services are not prerequisites.

# PR #122 revision plan

**Shape: Routine.** Remove one allocation capacity addition in existing code to resolve the reported CodeQL warning without changing metadata behavior.

## What we know

- CodeQL check `121411564420` reports allocation-size overflow at `internal/contract/types.go:226` (`.swarm/active/CI.md`); the operator identifies `go/allocation-size-overflow` and requests the smallest fix.
- `RoleAttestation.Metadata` allocates with `len(base)+8`, copies base entries, then adds nonempty attestation fields (`internal/contract/types.go:225`). The capacity hint does not determine returned map contents.
- `TestRoleAttestationMetadataKeepsBaseAndSkipsEmptyFields` checks preserved entries, nonempty field overrides, omitted empty fields, and input-map preservation (`internal/contract/attestation_test.go:8`).
- `ORIGINAL_PLAN.md` and `ORIGINAL_TEST_PLAN.md` remain the approved implementation context; `ACCEPTED_REVISIONS.md` lists no earlier deltas.

## What we're assuming

No functional change is needed beyond the capacity hint; confirm with the existing metadata test and required checks.

## Open questions

Whether CodeQL clears its diagnostic is verified by the next PR CodeQL run; local implementation and tests do not depend on access to that service.

## Revision delta and implementation

1. For the operator request and CodeQL check above, change only `RoleAttestation.Metadata` in `internal/contract/types.go:226` from `make(map[string]string, len(base)+8)` to `make(map[string]string, len(base))`. This removes length arithmetic from allocation sizing while preserving copying, overrides, and empty-field handling. Affected acceptance: criterion 1 (artifact metadata preservation), criterion 4 (attestation metadata for reuse evidence), and criterion 5 (existing tests and `make check` pass).
2. Run the verification in `TEST_PLAN.md`; inspect the source diff to confirm this is the only production change. Keep all validation-reuse logic, fencing, documentation, and protected files unchanged. CodeQL itself supplies the regression check for the removed overflow expression; do not add an infeasible huge-map runtime test.

This revision adds no changes to the original approved design beyond that allocation hint.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> CodeQL check fails on this PR with go/allocation-size-overflow (warning) at internal/contract/types.go:226, 'm := make(map[string]string, len(base)+8)' in RoleAttestation.Metadata: this PR's validation reuse decodes stored JSON metadata that now flows into that capacity expression. Fix with the smallest change: allocate without the arithmetic capacity hint (make(map[string]string, len(base)) or no hint) so no length arithmetic feeds the allocation. Do not change behavior; existing tests must still pass.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

Only the allocation hint changes. Retain the coverage in `ORIGINAL_TEST_PLAN.md` for all unchanged behavior.

| 2. Submit reuses only matching PASS evidence; otherwise validates | No selection logic changes; retain original criterion 2 coverage and run the full suite below. |
| 3. Dev builds never reuse | No version logic changes; retain original criterion 3 coverage and run the full suite below. |
| 4. Reuse is disclosed in output, artifacts, and PR descriptions | The metadata test above checks attestation merging; retain original criterion 4 output/provenance coverage and run the full suite below. |
| 5. Regression scenarios and `make check` pass | Run approved direct checks and `make check` below. Inspect the production diff for the single capacity-hint replacement. On the revised PR head, confirm CodeQL check `go/allocation-size-overflow` no longer reports `RoleAttestation.Metadata`. |

## Commands after implementation

```bash

unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
```
